gap: No result ChatGPT got states that an 18.5-inch 1920×1080 panel works out to 119 pixels per inch, with 10% fewer pixels spread over 27% more glass than a 16-inch 1920×1200 panel (141.5 PPI), nor what each added 18.5-inch screen costs ($193 to $367 on the stores read 2026-11-21).
standout_why: Compared against theofficejournal.com (attachable and for-work pages), itechguides.com and deal.ai's MagHub comparison, all opened 2026-11-21. The Office Journal tells readers to "calculate or look up the resulting pixel density" but gives no figure, and neither it nor itechguides names any 18-inch or 18.5-inch product (their largest is 16 inches). deal.ai lists the MagHub's resolution and 45 W input but no PPI, cost per screen or width. ChatGPT's own answer says 1080p at 18.5 inches looks "less sharp" without a number. I did not open Tom's Hardware, TechRadar, twelvetabs, gearlark or lbdsoftware, so the score is 2, not 3.
decides: It splits the question in two. For screens that are themselves 18.5 inches, Aura's Triple Boost Pro Studio 18.5" has the lowest cost per added screen of the stores read ($193.00), against $366.66 for the FOPO S999 at store price ($330.00 if code FOPO applies to it). So the 18.5-inch triple pick is Aura, not ours. For an extender that fits an 18-inch laptop, the FOPO S788 (FOPO's fit range is 12–18.5 inches) shows 11% more pixels per screen at 141.5 PPI for $180.00 per screen through our link. It honestly wins "most workspace per dollar on an 18-inch laptop", while the 18.5-inch 1080p panels win only on physical size (content drawn 19% larger). Two caveats on our rows: I could not open the S999 page (HTTP 429), and the only other linked row I can support is the S788, so the two-linked-rows rule is met only if the S999 gets a record.
